Scope-check PR #65 on the Zimmermann PWA Kit repo (/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa). Title: "feat(header): global header rebuild — shell, logo, Contentful nav data, close-state contract (SFCC-52/746/747)". Base commit 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99, head commit 10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d (both exist in the main repo's history; worktrees also exist at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/113175e9-2496-4539-9640-84df14f78583/scratchpad/pr65/{base,head} with node_modules symlinked in if you need to run anything). Get the diff yourself: `git diff 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99 10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d --stat` then drill into specific files as needed.

Judge whether the PR delivers exactly what its tickets ask — neither under- nor over-scope. Ground truth (Jira, already gathered — do not re-fetch):

SFCC-52 "Global Header UI" ACs (Desktop/Mobile unless marked):
1. Global header displayed at top of page, desktop and mobile. 2. Sticky on scroll. 3. Logo click navigates home. 4. Bag icon shows correct running item count. 5. Bag icon count updates live, no full reload. 6. (Desktop) All header icons (Search, Account, Saved, Bag) visible per Figma. 7. (Mobile) Hamburger top-left, Search + Bag top-right. 8. (Mobile) Tapping hamburger opens full-screen drawer, hamburger becomes close (×). 9. (Mobile) Tapping close (×) closes drawer, restores hamburger. 10. (Mobile) Drawer shows all top-level nav categories vertically, correct order. 11. (Mobile) Saved and Account links shown below main nav categories in the drawer.
Ticket description states: "Icon destinations (Search, Account, Wish List, Cart) are wired up as the underlying pages and features are built in their respective stories. The exception is the logo."
Important nuance: SFCC-52's own reporter (Tim Lavelle, who is also this PR's author) commented on the ticket suggesting AC4/5 (bag count) belong to a separate Cart story and AC8-11 belong to a Navigation story — but the Jira AC field itself was never edited to remove them, so they remain formally live ACs of record on this ticket today.

SFCC-746 "Navigation – PWA Kit & Contentful": supersedes the nav portion of SFCC-52. Nav items/order/storefront-visibility managed in Contentful, keyed by SFCC category taxonomy ID. Mega menu (desktop) and mobile hamburger/drill-down explicitly OUT of scope (covered by SFCC-96). Hover/focus/active visual states explicitly out of scope (defined in UI kit).

SFCC-747 "Logo Masthead": supersedes the logo portion of SFCC-52. ACs cover: left-aligned logo in its own row below nav (desktop/tablet/mobile); click navigates home; accessible name "Zimmermann" (alt or aria-label+role=img); link announced "Zimmermann, go to homepage"; **logo must be the FIRST focusable element in the header, before any nav items or icons**; visible 3:1-contrast focus ring. Scroll behaviour explicitly out of scope (SFCC-93). Logo is a static asset, not Contentful-managed, does not vary by storefront.

SFCC-96 "Expanded Navigation": desktop mega menu — hover/click a top-level nav item opens a full-width panel (left: subcategory + editorial links; right: campaign image; CLOSE control top-right), all Contentful-managed.

SFCC-97 "Expanded Navigation (Mobile)": hamburger → full nav panel, drill-down pattern with back control; Z.Immerse is a direct link (no drill-down); "Back in Boutique" included. **Archived 2026-08-24 as "all breakpoints covered in SFCC-96"** — SFCC-96 is now the ticket of record for this behaviour.

Specific scope questions to answer:
1. **Under-scope**: does the diff implement every AC above? Pay particular attention to SFCC-52 AC4/5 (bag icon live count) — check whether the new header actually wires up a live bag count anywhere, or whether it's genuinely just a static/visual icon per the ticket's own "destinations wired in their own stories" description. Either finding is fine — I need to know which it is, concretely, from the code.
2. **Over-scope**: this PR's commit history shows sub-branches merged in for SFCC-96 (mega menu) and SFCC-97 (mobile drill-down) — neither ticket was named in the review request (only 52/746/747), and both are Jira-assigned to a different person (Isabel Chaloner) than this PR's author (Tim Lavelle). Judge purely on the code and the tickets' own text: is the mega-menu/mobile-drawer implementation load-bearing for 52/746 to work coherently (e.g., can the nav bar/hamburger render and function sensibly with no mega-menu and no drill-down at all), or is it clearly separable, additional scope bundled into this one PR?
3. Any base SFCC template functionality removed or materially altered beyond what 52/746/747/96 require (AGENTS.md's "minimal changes" principle)?
4. Any of the ~104 changed files with no plausible connection to any of these 5 tickets?

Report your scope verdict: exactly right / under-scope (list every gap with the specific AC) / over-scope (list every addition with why it's beyond the named tickets) — cite file:line or file path for each item. Do not edit any code; report only.
